extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 40K video frames from video sequences across diverse environments, including crowded indoor and outdoor scenes with various lighting conditions.
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.citeAs: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi. HELVIPAD : A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation. arXiv:2411.18335v2, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two omnidirectional cameras in a vertical arrangement, paired with a synchronized LiDAR sensor. 29 video sequences were captured in dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes across a university campus, under diverse weather and lighting conditions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Given the sparse nature of LiDAR point clouds compared to high-resolution camera images, ground-truth depth labels cover only a fraction of the total pixels. Depth completion method does not provide labels for pixels at object boundaries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor mounted on a custom-built, remotely controlled robot chassis.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A fully automated depth completion pipeline tailored for 360° images. It interpolates depth on spherical grid points by using temporally aggregated point clouds (current frame plus 4 preceding and 4 succeeding frames) and applies a filtering process to exclude points with high uncertainty or lacking nearby measurements. Interpolation uses a weighted average of k-nearest neighbors.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Disparity values obtained from depth values via specific equation. Images cropped to remove unnecessary borders and downsized from a width of 1024 pixels to 512.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Mapping LiDAR to 360° Images via optimization of rotation and translation parameters to align LiDAR point clouds on the bottom equirectangular images. Hardware-triggered synchronization between sensors. Retaining one out of every three camera frames to match LiDAR frame rate. Cropping unnecessary regions (sky, ground).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Accurate depth and disparity labels created by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images. Depth completion pipeline applied to increase label density.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Alignment accuracy assessed by calculating pixel error (Euclidean distances) between 200 randomly selected LiDAR points and image positions, resulting in an average error of 1.7 pixels (8.0 pixels in challenging areas). Depth completion increases the ratio of labeled pixels from 12% to 61% while maintaining very low error rates.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, BFGS optimization algorithm
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Visual data of humans (pedestrians) in dynamic environments
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Facilitates development of mobile robots for real-world applications such as autonomous driving, healthcare, or agriculture, where accurate 3D representations of dynamic human environments are crucial for navigation and interaction.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Dataset collected on a university campus, potentially limiting diversity of environments. Indoor-trained models show a clear limitation in generalizing to outdoor scenes, particularly at night.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Sparse nature of LiDAR point clouds (ground-truth covers only a fraction of pixels). Limited for fast-moving objects like cars. Depth completion does not provide labels for pixels at object boundaries. Indoor-trained models struggle to generalize to outdoor/night scenes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Benchmarking for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models
